before.title: 1.6L Turbo 7-Speed Dry DCT Overheating, Shudder and Hesitation
before.description: The SX / GT-Line / X-Line turbo Seltos uses a 7-speed dry dual-clutch transmission (the base 2.0L uses an IVT/CVT). With no fluid bath to cool the clutch packs, the dry DCT can overheat in stop-and-go traffic, trigger a transmission-overheat warning, and enter a protect/limp mode. Owners also report low-speed judder, hesitation from a stop, and jerky engagement from heat-stressed dry clutches that can worsen as the unit warms.
before.solution: Apply Kia's DCT control-software (TCU) update that smooths clutch engagement and revises the overheat strategy. In heavy traffic, allow the unit to cool before resuming. Persistent shudder or repeated overheat warnings after the update point to worn dry-clutch packs needing replacement under powertrain warranty.
symptoms: Transmission overheat warning in slow traffic
Judder/shudder at low speed and crawl
Hesitation or lag from a stop
Temporary loss of drive / limp mode

proposal.title: Idle Stop & Go Oil Pump Overheating
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 23V531000 (Kia SC275) covers certain 2023-2024 Seltos vehicles equipped with an IVT and produced from November 9, 2022 through May 29, 2023. A supplier-damaged capacitor in the controller of the transmission's Idle Stop & Go electric oil pump can short while driving and cause thermal damage at the pump, increasing fire risk. Warning signs can include several driver-assistance or chassis warning lamps, an inoperative ISG system, limp-home mode, inability to turn off the engine, or smoke from the engine compartment.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for recall 23V531000. Until repaired, Kia recommends parking outdoors and away from other vehicles or structures. A Kia dealer inspects the electric oil pump assembly and, if necessary, replaces the electric oil pump controller free of charge. Do not substitute recall 23V578, disable ISG as a claimed remedy, or purchase radiator/coolant products for this electrical controller defect.
symptoms: Multiple chassis or driver-assistance warning lamps

before.description: Seltos owners across model years report moisture and water droplets forming inside the front LED headlight, DRL, and fog-lamp assemblies, often most visible after night driving when the lamps heat and then cool. proposal.title: Piston Oil Ring Defect and Engine Damage
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 25V099000 (Kia SC336) covers 53,635 certain 2021-2023 Seltos vehicles equipped with 2.0L Nu MPI engines and produced from July 2, 2020 through July 1, 2022. A supplier quality deviation can allow the piston oil ring to damage the cylinder wall, increasing oil consumption and eventually causing abnormal engine noise or an oil-pressure warning. If PNSS later sets P1327, the engine is replaced under the campaign. Kia's owner notice says that abnormal engine noise, the oil-pressure warning light or loss of drive power requires pulling over safely, not driving the vehicle and requesting a tow to a Kia dealer.

proposal.title: Stalling and Fire Hazard on Unrepaired / Still-Symptomatic 2021-2023 2.0L Vehicles
proposal.description: NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ25001 on August 6, 2025 to evaluate Kia's remedy for recall 25V099 after reviewing 47 complaints submitted from April 29 through June 27, 2025. Those complaints alleged an ineffective remedy, inconsistent engine-inspection results or unavailable remedies. The opening resume does not document 400-plus stalling complaints or four fires. Recall 25V099 itself says the piston-ring condition can cause increased oil consumption, abnormal engine noise or an oil-pressure warning and, if operation continues, engine seizure, loss of motive power or a limited fire risk.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN and arrange recall 25V099/SC336 service. If abnormal engine noise, the oil-pressure warning light or loss of drive power occurs, Kia's owner notice says to pull over safely, not drive and request towing to an authorized Kia dealer. If symptoms continue after service, inspection results conflict or the free remedy is unavailable, document the visits, contact Kia Customer Care and submit a complaint to NHTSA. The reviewed official documents do not direct every owner to park outside or make a lemon-law eligibility determination.
